title: 2 guns found near man shot and killed by Alberta RCMP
article: A 47-year-old man shot dead by police on a rural property near Morinville Friday night appeared to be in possession of two rifles.

According to the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which is now investigating the incident, two RCMP members were called to the property to investigate a trespassing complaint. Shortly after 8:15 p.m., the officers located an armed male in a field adjacent to the property.
When police attempted to deal with the man, a short confrontation occurred, prompting an officer to fire one shot. The man went down in the field, but officers could still see movement.

The scene turned into an armed standoff, prompting a call to the emergency response team (ERT). When attempts to communicate with the man went unsuccessful, the ERT approached the gunman and discovered he was dead.

ASIRT investigators rushed to the scene and recovered a loaded .22 calibre rifle near the man's body, along with a 30/30 lever action rifle nearby in the field. The carbine rifle fired by police was also seized.
The incident marks ASIRT's eighth officer-involved shooting since December 24, 2014. Four of those have been fatal.

Last week, a 31-year-old man armed with a sawed off shot gun was fatally shot by an Edmonton city police officer during a confrontation near Victoria Trail and Abbotsfield Road. The officer was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries to his lower body.
The Sun has learned the man has been identified as Michael David Perrault.
